    12  /-!
    13  # Termination of a hydra game
    14  
    15  This file deals with the following version of the hydra game: each head of the hydra is
    16  labelled by an element in a type `α`, and when you cut off one head with label `a`, it
    17  grows back an arbitrary but finite number of heads, all labelled by elements smaller than
    18  `a` with respect to a well-founded relation `r` on `α`. We show that no matter how (in
    19  what order) you choose cut off the heads, the game always terminates, i.e. all heads will
    20  eventually be cut off (but of course it can last arbitrarily long, i.e. takes an
    21  arbitrary finite number of steps).
    22  
    23  This result is stated as the well-foundedness of the `CutExpand` relation defined in
    24  this file: we model the heads of the hydra as a multiset of elements of `α`, and the
    25  valid "moves" of the game are modelled by the relation `CutExpand r` on `Multiset α`:
    26  `CutExpand r s' s` is true iff `s'` is obtained by removing one head `a ∈ s` and
    27  adding back an arbitrary multiset `t` of heads such that all `a' ∈ t` satisfy `r a' a`.
    28  
    29  We follow the proof by Peter LeFanu Lumsdaine at https://mathoverflow.net/a/229084/3332.
    30  
    31  TODO: formalize the relations corresponding to more powerful (e.g. Kirby–Paris and Buchholz)
    32  hydras, and prove their well-foundedness.
    33  -/
    34  
    35  @[expose] public section
    36  
    37  
    38  namespace Relation
    39  
    40  open Multiset Prod
    41  
    42  variable {α : Type*}
    43  
    44  /-- The relation that specifies valid moves in our hydra game. `CutExpand r s' s`
    45    means that `s'` is obtained by removing one head `a ∈ s` and adding back an arbitrary
    46    multiset `t` of heads such that all `a' ∈ t` satisfy `r a' a`.
    47  
    48    This is most directly translated into `s' = s.erase a + t`, but `Multiset.erase` requires
    49    `DecidableEq α`, so we use the equivalent condition `s' + {a} = s + t` instead, which
    50    is also easier to verify for explicit multisets `s'`, `s` and `t`.
    51  
    52    We also don't include the condition `a ∈ s` because `s' + {a} = s + t` already
    53    guarantees `a ∈ s + t`, and if `r` is irreflexive then `a ∉ t`, which is the
    54    case when `r` is well-founded, the case we are primarily interested in.
    55  
    56    The lemma `Relation.cutExpand_iff` below converts between this convenient definition
    57    and the direct translation when `r` is irreflexive. -/
    58  def CutExpand (r : α → α → Prop) (s' s : Multiset α) : Prop :=
    59    ∃ (t : Multiset α) (a : α), (∀ a' ∈ t, r a' a) ∧ s' + {a} = s + t
    60  
    61  variable {r : α → α → Prop}
    62  
    63  theorem cutExpand_le_invImage_lex [DecidableEq α] [Std.Irrefl r] :
    64      CutExpand r ≤ InvImage (Finsupp.Lex (rᶜ ⊓ (· ≠ ·)) (· < ·)) toFinsupp := by
    65    rintro s t ⟨u, a, hr, he⟩
    66    replace hr := fun a' ↦ mt (hr a')
    67    refine ⟨a, fun b h ↦ ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp_rw [toFinsupp_apply]
    68    · apply_fun count b at he
    69      simpa only [count_add, count_singleton, if_neg h.2, add_zero, count_eq_zero.2 (hr b h.1)]
    70        using he
    71    · apply_fun count a at he
    72      simp only [count_add, count_singleton_self, count_eq_zero.2 (hr _ (irrefl_of r a)),
    73        add_zero] at he
    74      exact he ▸ Nat.lt_succ_self _
